claims.text: CoFeNiTaAl-based magnetic HEAs can contain coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates dispersed in an FCC matrix.
Coherent nanoprecipitates in the CoFeNiTaAl-based system produce only a marginal coercivity increase of less than 10.7 Oe relative to the precipitate-free state.
Aging-temperature or cooling-rate adjustments can shift the nanoprecipitates from fully coherent to partially incoherent.
The modified heat treatment can preserve the overall FCC matrix while changing only precipitate-matrix interface coherency.
Partially incoherent precipitate interfaces introduce interfacial defects and local lattice distortions.
Interfacial defects and local lattice distortions at partially incoherent precipitates provide enhanced pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Incoherent interfaces disrupt the uniformity of magnetic exchange interactions.
Incoherent interfaces increase the energy barrier for magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Stronger domain-wall pinning caused by partially incoherent precipitates will increase coercivity.
The modified alloy will have a statistically measurable and significant coercive-field increase relative to a coherently precipitated baseline.
The baseline consists of coherent, ordered nanoprecipitates associated with a coercivity increase below 10.7 Oe.
The coercivity-enhancing effect should hold only if coherency is altered without deleterious phase transformations or loss of the FCC matrix.
Excessive microstructural disruption may degrade both mechanical and magnetic properties.
The magnitude of the coercivity change may depend on complex interactions between mechanical strengthening and domain-wall pinning.
TEM can be used to compare precipitate-interface coherency between the two sample sets.
Magnetic hysteresis measurements by VSM or SQUID can provide the coercive field.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant coercivity increase relative to the matched coherent-precipitate baseline would falsify the predicted outcome.
Finding that the modified samples remain coherent despite treatment would itself falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention is defined as successfully shifting precipitates toward partial incoherency, but the falsification rule treats failure to achieve that manipulation as falsification of the causal hypothesis. Remaining coherent demonstrates an unsuccessful intervention rather than testing the effect of partial incoherency on coercivity.
